newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH SPT PROPOSES 10 FOR ONE STOCK SPLIT.
newsitem.headline: CZECH SPT PROPOSES 10 FOR ONE STOCK SPLIT.

text.p: The board of Czech fixed-line telephone monopoly SPT Telecom a.s. will propose a 10 for one split of its common stock at the annual general meeting of shareholders on June 20, SPT chief financial officer Urs Kamber said on Monday.
The plan, if approved, would exchange one share of SPT stock with an original nominal value of 1,000 crowns, for 10 new shares with a nominal value of 100 crowns.
Kamber told Reuters the move was intended to add liquidity on the secondary market to pricey SPT shares, which have been trading at over 3,000 crowns for much of the past year.
"It's a heavy stock at this point. We've looked at other (telephone) operators in Europe and we've found that (SPT shares) are five to 10 times more expensive," Kamber said.
SPT shares were trading at mid-session at 3,180 crowns, 50 crowns lower than Friday's close on the Prague Stock Exchange.

SPT shares rose to trade in the 3,000 crown range from just above 2,000 crowns after a 27 percent stake in the former state monopoly was privatised in the summer of 1995 to a consortium comprised of Dutch and Swiss PTT operators.
SPT posted a 483 million crown 1996 net loss as the company made one-off moves to provision itself against structural changes after a 4.83 billion crown net profit for 1995.
The firm posted the loss, according to international accounting standards (IAS), due to one- time extraordinary charges of 8.757 billion crowns.
About 1.75 billion crowns of this was taken as the firm prepares for layoffs and restructuring that should see SPT shed some 10,000 of its current 26,800 workforce by the year 2000.
SPT's annual meeting is set for 10 a.m. (0800 GMT) on June 20 at the Zofin centre in Prague.
